rubric.aggregation: macro mean of per-query scores within each split and scenario

grade_rules.0: all remaining pairs; omitted from sparse qrels inside the declared corpus universe
grade_rules.1: >= 2 shared core ingredients and core coverage >= 0.30
grade_rules.2: protein match when applicable; >= 2 shared core ingredients; core coverage >= 0.45; query utility >= 0.50
grade_rules.3: protein match when query has protein; core coverage >= 0.65; query utility >= 0.60

rubric.known_item_limit: sampled ingredient subsets may match many recipes and need not identify a unique target
rubric.known_item_relevance: declared target doc_id only; shared ingredients do not prove duplicate recipes
rubric.latency_limit: one retrieval call per query without warm-up; descriptive only
rubric.limitations: Heuristic ingredient rubric overlaps Hybrid core coverage, query utility, and protein alignment; proxy scores measure rubric agreement, not human relevance. Corpus-derived synthetic queries do not establish real-user performance.

metric_definitions.AP@10: sum of precision at relevant ranks in top 10 / min(10, total relevant)
metric_definitions.P@k: relevant returned in top k / k
metric_definitions.R@k: relevant returned in top k / all relevant in proxy assessment universe
metric_definitions.RR@10: reciprocal rank of first grade >= 2 within top 10, else zero
metric_definitions.nDCG@k: gain 2**grade - 1 with log2(rank + 1) discount; ideal from all qrels

rubric.model_feature_limit: TF-IDF also uses titles; model differences are not algorithm-only
rubric.noisy_scenario: synthetic quantities and selected culinary aliases, not typo correction
rubric.proxy_qrel_input: clean reference ingredients; retrieval receives the original query
rubric.split_limit: exact family grouping only; inspected synthetic queries are not an untouched holdout
rubric.zero_denominator_policy: score zero and retain query in macro average; report counts
